exposure: Mode of birth (caesarean, home delivery, outside health facility)
cohort: The study analyzed data from 5122 children derived from the Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey 2016.
finding: The study identified that various socio-demographic, economic, and healthcare factors were significantly associated with early initiation of breastfeeding, exclusive breastfeeding, and the overall duration of breastfeeding in Ethiopia.
mod_finding: Caesarean birth and home delivery were associated with a lower likelihood of early initiation of breastfeeding, while giving birth outside of health facilities was linked to non-exclusive and shorter durations of breastfeeding.
cross-section timing: Data extracted from the Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey 2016
birth_weight: Average/larger size of a child at birth was associated with non-exclusive breastfeeding, and small birthweight babies with late initiation of breastfeeding.
